title: Reconciliation: comparing old and new trees

slides.say: Each update gives React a new tree of elements. It must find the cheapest way to update the screen.

slides.text: Exact tree diffing is O(n³): 1,000 elements ≈ a billion comparisons.
slides.say: A perfect diff of two trees is very expensive. For one thousand elements, around a billion comparisons. Far too slow.

slides.text: React uses an O(n) heuristic with 2 assumptions: different types → different trees; keys mark stable children.
slides.say: So React uses a fast, linear heuristic, based on two assumptions. Elements of different types produce different trees. And keys hint which children stay the same.

slides.text: It’s an implementation detail: the result is the same as re-rendering everything.
slides.say: Reconciliation is an implementation detail. The result is the same as if React re-rendered the whole app. It just applies only the differences.
